Geo Eval Harness Geospatial Foundation Model Ranking

Geospatial foundation models are pretrained backbones, with the promise of being easily adaptable to various earth observation downstream tasks. Geo Eval Harness is a collective effort to provide transparent and fair evaluations of these models on established protocols such that the community can gain a better understanding of model performance across tasks.

The table summarizes per-dataset scores, and four settings provide different views of the results:

  • Aggregation sets how the per-dataset scores are combined into a single number.
  • Task switches between classification (per-image label) and segmentation (per-pixel mIoU) benchmarks.
  • Probe sets how frozen embeddings become predictions for classification: a fitted linear classifier or KNN-5.
  • For segmentation, Adaptation sets what trains with the decoder (frozen backbone, LoRA, or full fine-tuning), Decoder the head (UPerNet or U-Net), and Pyramid how the multi-scale features are built (the backbone's native features, a ViT neck, or AnyUp upsampling). Each dataset uses its canonical training protocol; Show variants adds the other epoch and backbone learning-rate setups. Cells are the mean over seeds, with the standard deviation and seed count underneath.
  • Bands sets the input modality for the backbone that configures the required bands and order, either RGB or the available multispectral channels. For segmentation, Native bands ranks each model on its own input bands per dataset (RGB, multispectral or SAR), merging a model's per-modality configurations; the Default pyramid is each model's own (native features or ViT neck).

Each setting is a separate experiment rather than a filter applied to one result, so the table can reorder when you change one of them. A model is ranked only when it has a result on every eligible dataset in the selected view, and the models that fall short are named below the table. Native-bands segmentation views are the exception: each model is ranked on the datasets it has, and the Datasets column shows how many. The evaluation setup documents the protocol, the coverage rules, and how each aggregation is computed.

If a result looks wrong, is missing, or seems implausible, please open an issue with the model, the view you were looking at, and any supporting evidence. General feedback is of course welcome too.

Ranking sensitivity across views

Pick which experiments to compare, using average rank. Each cell asks whether the same models land in the same order in two views: it keeps only models available in both, re-ranks them using every dataset available in each, and then calculates tie-aware Kendall τ-b. +1 means the same order, 0 little agreement, and −1 a reversal.

Each cell reports τ-b, shared models (n), and datasets in its row and column views (d). A dagger marks a small shared roster — read those cells with caution, especially across tasks where few models overlap.
